speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly what happens when you wake up frightened at night, and how old are you? I understand you are 8 years old; does this happen every night or only occasionally?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder.

Based on the description of waking up frightened, yelling, and crying with the ability to be consoled and lack of confusion, this presentation is consistent with nightmares rather than sleep terrors. The frequency (1-2 times per week) and duration (2 months) also support this diagnosis. Do you have any concerns about her recent stressors or trauma?
